acceptance: The product selects exactly one Run Summary owner surface (independent screen, HUD overlay, or MainMenu metadata panel), and leaving ownership undefined or split across multiple surfaces fails acceptance. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0066AcceptanceTests.cs

The chosen Run Summary surface displays outcome, difficulty, node progress, and failure or recovery reason from stored run metadata, and opening the surface does not recompute, derive, or mutate run state. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/UI/test_run_summary_surface.gd Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0066AcceptanceTests.cs

For the same saved run, the chosen Run Summary surface shows difficulty and continue-related metadata that match the HUD difficulty display and Continue metadata, and mismatched or stale values fail acceptance. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Tasks/test_task0045_acceptance.gd Tests.Godot/tests/UI/test_run_summary_surface.gd Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0066AcceptanceTests.cs
description: Decide and wire the run summary surface so outcome, difficulty, progress, and recovery metadata are shown without recomputing run state.
test_strategy: Add a focused UI test for the chosen Run Summary surface and consistency with HUD/Continue metadata.
title: Define and implement run summary surface ownership

acceptance: The existing Shop scene must be bound to real route-owned behavior so the player can perform purchase, remove, transform/reforge, and leave actions from the actual Shop UI, and each action must resolve through the Shop-owned route instead of placeholder or unowned behavior. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Shop/test_shop_scene_behavior_binding.gd Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0067AcceptanceTests.cs

The Shop UI must expose the observable state needed for real shop actions, including current offers, prices, player gold/resources, and owned/removed outcomes, and it must show a visible failure reason when a purchase cannot be completed because resources are insufficient or the offer was already taken. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Shop/test_shop_scene_behavior_binding.gd Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0067AcceptanceTests.cs

When the player re-enters Shop through the run flow, the locked Shop inventory must remain unchanged, and duplicate purchases or invalid offer ids must be refused with visible feedback instead of silently succeeding or mutating state. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Tasks/test_task0020_acceptance.gd Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_reward_shop_event_resume_determinism.gd

Shop player-facing UI text and Shop-related service text must stay within Shop semantics and must not present upgrade, rest, campfire, or card-upgrade context. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Shop/test_shop_scene_behavior_binding.gd Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0067AcceptanceTests.cs

Completing or leaving Shop must return the run to Map through the same explicit route ownership model used for Map-to-node entry, rather than through an ad hoc or separate return path. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Shop/test_shop_scene_behavior_binding.gd

At least one real-scene Shop behavior binding test must execute against the actual Shop scene and verify purchase, remove, transform/reforge, and leave behavior on that scene, not only through mocks or pure unit seams. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Shop/test_shop_scene_behavior_binding.gd Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0067AcceptanceTests.cs

At least one Windows route roundtrip check must verify that Map-to-Shop entry and Shop-to-Map return use the same route ownership model in both directions. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Shop/test_shop_scene_behavior_binding.gd Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0067AcceptanceTests.cs
description: Bind the existing Shop scene to real purchase, remove, transform, leave, and no-upgrade-context behavior with explicit route ownership.
test_strategy: Add a real-scene Shop behavior binding test and route roundtrip check on Windows.
title: Implement real Shop UI behavior binding and route ownership

acceptance: M1 run-entry, map, node, reward, rest, shop, combat, and continue surfaces must expose primary actions that can be invoked by keyboard and controller input. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_m1_ui_focus_accessibility.gd Tests.Godot/tests/UI/A11y/test_button_invokable.gd

Focus traversal across the M1 critical-path run-entry, map, node, reward, rest, shop, combat, and continue surfaces must reach each required action without trapping focus or skipping required actions. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/UI/A11y/test_focus_cycle.gd Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0068AcceptanceTests.cs

Primary actions on the M1 run-entry, map, node, reward, rest, shop, combat, and continue surfaces must keep visible labels that identify the action being invoked. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/UI/A11y/test_visible_labels.gd Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_m1_ui_focus_accessibility.gd

The existing A11y UI tests for button invocation, focus cycling, and visible labels must run as the deterministic verification gate for Task 68. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/UI/A11y/test_button_invokable.gd Tests.Godot/tests/UI/A11y/test_focus_cycle.gd Tests.Godot/tests/UI/A11y/test_visible_labels.gd

After the P0/P1 UI surfaces required for the M1 critical path exist, one focus smoke covering that path must be added and included in the deterministic verification gate. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_m1_ui_focus_accessibility.gd Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0068AcceptanceTests.cs
description: Batch the P2 accessibility and focus-cycle work for the M1 run-entry, map, node, reward, rest, shop, combat, and continue surfaces.
test_strategy: Run existing A11y UI tests and add one M1 critical-path focus smoke after P0/P1 UI surfaces exist.
title: Implement M1 UI focus and accessibility pass

acceptance: Before the player confirms an Event choice, the Event scene displays the event title, description, available options, and each option's visible cost or reward preview. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Event/test_event_scene_result_feedback.gd Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0069AcceptanceTests.cs

After the player commits a choice, the Event scene displays the chosen option, a result summary, and the resulting numeric changes for affected stats or rewards such as HP, gold, status, cards, or relics. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Event/test_event_scene_result_feedback.gd Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0069AcceptanceTests.cs

When an Event resolves, the flow returns to Reward or Map through the same route-owned node resolution path used by the M1 map flow. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_m1_node_resolution_routes.gd

If an Event choice is invalid or unavailable, the player remains in the Event scene, receives visible blocked-state feedback, and no game state changes are applied. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0069AcceptanceTests.cs

All player-visible Event copy is delivered through translation keys, and choice presentation does not omit or hide cost information. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Event/test_event_scene_hp_loss_cost_applies_immediately.gd Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Event/test_event_scene_curse_card_cost_applies_immediately.gd

A real-scene Event result feedback test verifies that, after commit, the chosen option, the result summary, and the resulting numeric changes are visible to the player. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Event/test_event_scene_result_feedback.gd Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0069AcceptanceTests.cs

A Windows route-return smoke verifies that completing an Event returns to Reward or Map through the route-owned node resolution model. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_m1_node_resolution_routes.gd Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0069AcceptanceTests.cs
description: Complete Event node UX so costs, choices, results, blocked states, and return-to-map behavior are player-visible and route-owned.
test_strategy: Add one real-scene Event result feedback test and one route-return smoke on Windows.
title: Implement Event result explainability and node feedback routing

acceptance: On M1 Map, the player-facing entry presents a connected route graph with visible legal-transition edges, continues to use the existing route-owned Map-to-node transition flow, does not present the four standalone node-type shortcut buttons as the primary entry path, and does not introduce any parallel Map-to-node transition owner or second execution path. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Map/test_map_tree_route.gd

The M1 route graph must expose a deterministic directed edge set for the full five-floor route: every non-terminal node has at least one legal outgoing edge to the next floor, the final node has no outgoing edge, and no edge skips floors or points to an undefined node ID. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Map/test_map_tree_route.gd

Map rendering makes reachable, locked, completed, and selected-path states visually distinguishable on both nodes and edges so currently legal choices are directly observable. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Map/test_map_tree_route.gd

Selecting a reachable node triggers the existing route-owned Map-to-node transition; selecting a locked or disconnected node shows visible refusal feedback, does not transition, and keeps run progression unchanged. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Map/test_map_tree_route.gd

After node completion, route-graph reachability updates so only legal next-floor nodes and connecting edges become reachable, while traversed segments remain visible as completed path history. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Map/test_map_tree_route.gd

When route-graph entry is active, legacy ActionRow shortcut buttons (Combat, Event, Shop, Rest) are hidden or removed from the player-facing Map. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Map/test_map_tree_route.gd

Route-node selection must have a single execution authority: reachable-node selection resolves exactly once through the existing route-owned transition path, while locked/disconnected selections resolve to refusal feedback only and never invoke an alternative scene transition path. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Map/test_map_tree_route.gd

Workflow-selection gate evidence for T70 must be recorded before implementation evidence is accepted; verification must assert a concrete workflow-selection summary artifact exists with task_id=70 and that its timestamp is not later than the selected implementation evidence timestamp. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0070AcceptanceTests.cs
description: Upgrade the existing Map route-owned flow with a connected route graph that shows legal path edges, locked paths, completed path history, and current reachable choices.
test_strategy: Extend the existing Map route GdUnit suite to cover connected route graph edges, path-state visualization, legal unlock progression, and hidden legacy shortcut buttons on Windows.
title: Upgrade Map route graph visualization on top of existing route ownership

acceptance: T80 is accepted only when evidence from the shared DeckService/CardState runtime path shows deterministic combat deck-lifecycle outcomes for draw-pile-to-hand draw, turn-end discard into discard pile, exhaust-pile placement, and discard-to-draw reshuffle ordering. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Services/DeckServiceTests.cs Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

T81 is accepted only when Combat scene/HUD wiring remains synchronized with runtime transitions for draw, hand, discard, and exhaust states, and scene code is limited to binding/orchestration without taking scene-local deck-lifecycle ownership or duplicating lifecycle logic. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Services/DeckServiceTests.cs Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

T82 can close this umbrella milestone only when Windows-run evidence from existing deck-lifecycle and Combat scene suites aggregates T80 and T81 results; introducing a fourth parallel implementation path or standalone duplicate track fails acceptance. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

The aggregated T80-T82 milestone evidence must explicitly verify hand state, exhaust pile, turn-end discard behavior, deterministic ordering, and Windows-backed execution, in addition to draw/discard/reshuffle behavior and HUD synchronization. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Services/DeckServiceTests.cs Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

T71 remains milestone-only: validation must run through existing DeckService and Combat scene suites, and acceptance fails if a replacement verification lane or a fourth implementation path is used. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Services/DeckServiceTests.cs Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

No implementation evidence under this task is valid unless workflow selection of T71 is recorded first, and the review evidence set must include that selection record before implementation evidence. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0071WorkflowSelectionEvidenceTests.cs
description: Use this task only as the combat deck-lifecycle umbrella above T80-T82, with implementation carried by the concrete shared-runtime slices instead of a parallel scene-local rework.
test_strategy: Validate this milestone by aggregating T80-T82 evidence from existing DeckService and Combat scene suites; do not add a separate implementation-only test slice under T71.
title: Consolidate combat deck lifecycle wiring as the umbrella task for T80-T82

acceptance: When CombatScene renders playable cards, each card button shows localized card name, cost, card type, and player-visible effect summary sourced from the existing card-definition and translation contracts, with no hard-coded scene text and no parallel card text/model source. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0072AcceptanceTests.cs

Playing any damage, block, status, or mixed-effect card resolves strictly from its existing card definition (including cost payment, targeting rule, and exhaust/discard routing); for each effect component, only definition-allowed targets are mutated and non-target entities remain unchanged, and resulting HP, block, energy, and pile states match that definition. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0072AcceptanceTests.cs

Each successful card play emits visible player-facing feedback that matches the resolved outcomes, including damage dealt, block gained, statuses applied, and whether the card was exhausted or discarded. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_feedback_log.gd Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0072AcceptanceTests.cs

If play is rejected due to insufficient energy, missing card definition, or invalid targeting rule, the UI presents refusal feedback and leaves HP, block, energy, and pile states unchanged. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_feedback_log.gd Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0072AcceptanceTests.cs

On the M1 combat surface, both en and zh-CN must render localized card name and localized card body/effect description for playable cards (including Strike and Defend) from the existing translation + card-definition contracts, with visible cost/type data from the same existing definition path; raw localization keys or placeholder text are not allowed. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_m1_visible_text_flow.gd Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0072AcceptanceTests.cs

CombatScene reads card type from existing card definitions and uses that type for combat presentation and interaction behavior, without hard-coded fallback typing or any parallel card-description path. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0072AcceptanceTests.cs

When a status card is played, the defined status is applied to the correct target, and when an exhaust-effect card is played, that card is moved to exhaust (not discard) per the existing definition path. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_feedback_log.gd Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0072AcceptanceTests.cs

CombatScene card loading uses only existing contracts and current card data files, and does not introduce any new card-definition path or new card-data file family. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0072AcceptanceTests.cs

Legacy hard-coded Strike/Defend UI/effect wiring is removed from CombatScene runtime behavior: rendering, cost display, targeting, and resolution for Strike/Defend must come from the same existing card definition + localization + effect contracts path as all other cards, without card-specific hard-coded branches. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_feedback_log.gd Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0072AcceptanceTests.cs

Before workflow selection evidence marks Task 72 as selected, CombatScene implementation changes for this task must not be executable/claimed as delivered; once selected, implementation evidence must trace to the same existing card-definition + localization + effect-contract path (no parallel model path). Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0072AcceptanceTests.cs

For target-rule edge cases (self-only, enemy-only, and invalid selected target), CombatScene must apply or refuse strictly per existing card targeting contracts, with refusal feedback and unchanged state on invalid selection. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_feedback_log.gd Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0072AcceptanceTests.cs
description: Wire CombatScene to existing data-driven card definitions, localized card text, costs, targeting rules, and effect resolution instead of extending hard-coded Strike and Defend behavior.
test_strategy: Extend Combat scene binding and feedback suites to cover data-driven card definitions, localized text, effect summaries, and refusal paths.
title: Bind CombatScene to existing data-driven card definitions and localized card text

acceptance: In multi-enemy runtime state, Combat must expose every living legal runtime enemy as a selectable and inspectable target entry, and each exposed enemy must surface name, HP, block, status, and intent. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

Card play must enforce legal targeting: single-target cards resolve only when a living legal enemy is selected, and on success the effect applies to the selected enemy only; non-selected enemies must remain unchanged unless the card explicitly declares all-enemy/global behavior, while self-target and all-enemy cards resolve without selecting an enemy. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Battle/test_battle_card_targeting_drag_play_flow.gd Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

If the selected target is invalid, dead, locked, or disconnected, card play must be rejected with visible feedback, and HP, energy, and pile state must stay unchanged. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Battle/test_battle_card_targeting_drag_play_flow.gd

When an enemy dies, it must be removed from the legal target set, and the remaining enemies must keep deterministic combat state with intent still visible. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

After all enemies are defeated, combat completion must remain route-owned and must transition to Reward or Map based on current node rules. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_m1_visible_text_flow.gd

Combat victory routing must not trigger while any legal living enemy remains; route-owned completion may execute only after the legal living enemy set becomes empty. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_m1_visible_text_flow.gd

If the currently selected enemy becomes dead, disconnected, or otherwise illegal before card resolution, Combat must clear or deterministically retarget selection and must never resolve card effects against an illegal target. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Battle/test_battle_card_targeting_drag_play_flow.gd Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd
description: Extend the current combat targeting and victory-routing skeleton so cards resolve against legal enemies, dead enemies leave the target set, and multi-enemy combat completion stays route-owned.
test_strategy: Extend Combat and targeting flow suites to cover legal target resolution, invalid target refusal, enemy death, and combat completion routing.
title: Upgrade existing combat targeting and victory routing to multi-enemy runtime state

acceptance: Dragging a card from hand onto a legal target and releasing it must issue the play request through the current validated card-play path (the same path used by click-based play). Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/UI/test_card_drag_target_play.gd Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Battle/test_battle_card_targeting_drag_play_flow.gd

While a dragged card is hovering a legal target, the UI shows a visible target highlight/preview, and no combat state change is applied before release. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/UI/test_card_drag_target_play.gd

Dropping on an invalid target or empty area does not commit play: visible invalid/cancel feedback is shown, the card returns to hand, and energy plus pile state remain unchanged. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Battle/test_battle_card_targeting_drag_play_flow.gd

The click path and Play Selected Card accessibility path both remain usable, and a successful legal activation is behaviorally equivalent to a successful legal drag release through the same play flow. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd
Drag preview and target-hover interactions are UI-only and must not advance combat RNG streams or route progression. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/UI/test_card_drag_target_play.gd

Keyboard fallback and controller fallback must each complete target selection and play via the same validated card-play path as drag release, without introducing a separate combat input stack. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

Implementation for this task proceeds only after workflow explicitly selects T74, and review evidence includes that workflow-selection record before implementation evidence. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0074WorkflowSelectionEvidenceTests.cs
description: Add mouse drag, target hover, release-to-play, cancel, and invalid-target feedback on top of the current targeting path while preserving click or button accessibility fallback.
test_strategy: Promote existing drag-target harness coverage into real Combat scene behavior tests, including valid drop, invalid drop, cancel, and accessibility fallback.
title: Upgrade existing targeting flow with Slay-the-Spire-style card drag UX

acceptance: When player or enemy statuses are active in combat (including strength, weak, vulnerable, block, poison, and temporary modifiers), each active status is shown on the combat surface with a readable label, visible stack/value, and decision-useful tooltip/detail text, and no active status is omitted. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

Given the same initial combat state and action sequence, damage and mitigation results are identical across repeated runs, and contributions from strength, weak, vulnerable, block-like effects, poison ticks, and temporary modifiers come from the existing status/modifier rule path. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

At turn boundaries, status apply/stack/decay/expire changes are reflected in HUD/feedback within the same turn flow, so the current status state is fully readable from UI feedback without log inspection. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_feedback_log.gd

If combat encounters an invalid or expired status reference, the invalid effect is rejected, visible failure feedback is emitted, and combat state remains non-corrupted and playable. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_feedback_log.gd
On M1 combat surfaces, status-related UI text renders correctly in en and zh-CN and never exposes raw localization keys. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

Status rendering, damage/mitigation resolution, and turn-boundary decay all execute through the shared existing status contracts/services path, with no UI-local rule path used for those outcomes. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_feedback_log.gd

UI-only modules do not define parallel status semantics for stacking, decay, or modifier computation; presence of a parallel UI status-rule path fails this task. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

Implementation evidence for T75 is valid only if workflow-selection evidence explicitly selecting T75 appears first; if selection evidence is missing or appears after implementation evidence, acceptance fails. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0075WorkflowSelectionEvidenceTests.cs
description: Expose the existing player and enemy status-effect foundations as visible combat state such as strength, weak, vulnerable, block, poison, and temporary modifiers with deterministic updates.
test_strategy: Extend Combat UI binding and feedback tests to cover status rendering, status-modified damage/block resolution, and turn-boundary decay.
title: Wire existing status contracts and rules into visible combat status effects

acceptance: Before any player action, the existing intent surface renders enemy intent generated from enemy AI behavior definitions as the single source (no fixed/hardcoded fallback preview), and the rendered intent can express attack, block, buff, debuff, and mixed intent outputs. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

Enemy behavior selection for intent preview uses the named combat RNG stream, while UI-only interactions (hover, drag preview, localization refresh) leave that stream state unchanged; this task covers intent generation/preview only and does not execute enemy action resolution or no-repeat guardrail enforcement. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

With the same deterministic inputs, the upgraded intent path produces repeatable enemy intent output, and this determinism is verifiable without invoking enemy turn execution or action-resolution paths. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

T76 scope is limited to enemy intent generation and preview binding; enemy action resolution and no-repeat guardrail enforcement are explicitly out of scope for T76 acceptance paths. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

The upgrade reuses the existing intent surface nodes and binding points; no parallel replacement intent surface is introduced in this task. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

Under deterministic seed/inputs, enemy intent preview generated from AI behavior definitions remains repeatable and visible on existing intent surfaces, and UI-only operations do not advance the named combat RNG stream. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd
description: Replace fixed enemy attack preview with data-driven intent generation and preview while deferring enemy action resolution and no-repeat guardrails to a follow-up task.
test_strategy: Extend Combat scene tests to cover deterministic enemy intent generation, visible preview, and UI-only RNG non-advancement on the upgraded intent path.
title: Bind enemy intent generation and preview to data-driven AI on existing intent surfaces

acceptance: On the shared combat runtime path, trigger registration and execution order is deterministic for card-play, turn-start, turn-end, damage, and death-check hooks; repeated identical runs produce identical hook order and outcomes, and no second trigger stack is used. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

Card-play, turn-start, turn-end, damage, and death-check hooks are each invoked on the shared combat runtime path and produce deterministic end-to-end outputs for identical command sequences (feedback/history ordering and state deltas). Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_feedback_log.gd

The shared combat runtime exposes one auditable trigger-registration path, and trigger execution consumes registrations only from that shared path, not from side-channel or duplicate stacks. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

After integrating these hooks, combat completion ownership remains in the route flow; trigger processing must not finalize or redirect route completion on its own, and death-check outcomes must be consumed through the existing route-owned completion chain. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_feedback_log.gd

This task introduces no powers/relics/potions presentation wiring and no powers/relics/potions effect integration into runtime hook execution; related behavior remains absent/deferred in this phase. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_feedback_log.gd

When damage is lethal, death-check hook executes exactly once after damage resolution and before route-owned completion consumption; trigger processing itself must not finalize or redirect route completion. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_feedback_log.gd
On non-lethal damage resolution, death-check hook is not executed and route-owned completion flow remains unchanged. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_feedback_log.gd
description: Integrate deterministic trigger registration and card-play, turn, damage, and death-check hooks into combat runtime while deferring powers/relics/potions presentation and effect integration to a follow-up task.
test_strategy: Add deterministic trigger-order assertions through existing Combat scene suites for card-play, turn, damage, and death-check hooks on the shared runtime path.
title: Integrate trigger registration and combat-time hooks into the shared combat runtime

acceptance: For every successful card play and every resolved enemy action, the presentation layer must emit the transient visible feedback applicable to that resolved outcome (including damage numbers, block gain numbers, card-play motion cues, and hit/action feedback where relevant) in addition to HUD updates, and deterministic combat outcomes must remain identical to baseline runs. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_combat_scene_ui_bindings.gd

When card play, hit, block, invalid action, or enemy action runtime events occur, the corresponding combat SFX hook must be triggered; if an audio asset is missing, action resolution must still complete safely and required visible feedback must still be produced (audio playback may explicitly no-op) without runtime failure. acceptance: A shared runtime producer such as a relic or event can register deterministic add, remove, or mutate reward-entry modifications for the next reward context before snapshot generation, and when that next context is first materialized those registered modifications are applied without editing the underlying reward pool file. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0133AcceptanceTests.cs

After reward_pool_id resolution and before reward snapshot lock, the pipeline applies the registered add, remove, and mutate operations to the entry list that becomes the next context snapshot, and the first reward-scene entry shows that modified result. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0133AcceptanceTests.cs Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_m1_visible_text_flow.gd

If a reward context is already locked in the shared reward owner path, later runtime modifiers leave that existing snapshot unchanged; a later still-unlocked context using the same reward pool id starts from the unmodified pool baseline and only applies modifiers newly registered for that later context when it is first materialized. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0133AcceptanceTests.cs Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_reward_offer_lock_persist_reenter.gd

The runtime modifier pipeline preserves deterministic replay and reward lock semantics: identical shared run inputs produce the same modified reward snapshot, and re-entering the same reward context returns the unchanged locked modified snapshot. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0133AcceptanceTests.cs Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_reward_offer_lock_persist_reenter.gd

Registered reward-entry modifiers are consumed only by the next reward context they target: once a context is first materialized or locked, those modifiers do not bleed into later contexts unless those later contexts register their own modifiers. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0133AcceptanceTests.cs Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_m1_visible_text_flow.gd

Runtime modifiers are limited to governed add, remove, and mutate changes within the existing reward entry schema, and attempts to submit unsupported reward types or partially invalid entry payloads fail explicitly or are surfaced explicitly without partially mutating the target reward snapshot. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Tasks/Task0133AcceptanceTests.cs
description: Build a governed hook between reward-pool selection and reward-snapshot locking so relics, events, and other run-state systems can add, remove, or mutate reward entries for the next reward context without editing pool files.
test_strategy: Add xUnit and GdUnit coverage for pre-snapshot modifier registration, deterministic next-context application, already-locked context immutability, and visible reward-scene results after modifier application.
